documents.prompt: Graph $f(x)={{a}}(x-{{h}})^2{{k|signed}}$ by plotting its vertex, then write the domain and range.

solutionReview.headline: An upward-opening quadratic extends forever left and right but has a lowest output.
reasoning: There is no restriction on x, so the domain is all real numbers.
The vertex $({{h}},{{k}})$ is the minimum, so the range is $[{{k}},\infty)$.

attemptFeedback: Separate horizontal extent (domain) from vertical extent (range).
supportHints: The vertex gives the range endpoint; the parabola continues indefinitely in both x-directions.

documents.prompt: A projectile is modeled by $h(t)=-{{a}}(t-{{v}})^2+{{maxh}}$ only from launch until it returns to the ground. Write the reasonable domain of time and the corresponding range of height in interval notation.

solutionReview.headline: Context can restrict a quadratic that is mathematically defined for every real input.
reasoning: Because {{maxh}}={{a}}({{v}})^2, the model reaches ground level at t=0 and t={{end}}.
During the physical flight, time runs from 0 to {{end}} and height runs from 0 to the vertex height {{maxh}}.

attemptFeedback: Use the physical interval of flight, not the unrestricted algebraic domain of the formula.
supportHints: The vertex occurs halfway between the two ground times.

documents.prompt: For $q(x)={{a}}(x-{{h}})^2{{k|signed}}$ restricted to ${{h}}\le x\le {{hi}}$, write BOTH the domain and range in interval notation.

solutionReview.headline: A restricted domain changes the range because only part of the parabola is allowed.
reasoning: The domain starts at the vertex x={{h}} and ends at {{hi}}.
On this right-hand branch the function increases from {{k}} to {{top}}, so the range is $[{{k}},{{top}}]$.

attemptFeedback: Evaluate the function at the restricted endpoint as well as at the vertex.
supportHints: Because the domain begins at the vertex and moves right, the outputs increase.

variants.prompt: For $q(x)={{a}}(x-{{h}})^2{{k|signed}}$ restricted to ${{lo}}\le x\le {{hi}}$, determine the domain and range. The interval crosses the vertex, so evaluate the vertex and BOTH restricted endpoints before deciding the maximum output.

solutionReview.headline: When a restricted interval crosses the vertex, compare the vertex with both endpoint outputs.
reasoning: The vertex x={{h}} lies inside [{{lo}},{{hi}}], so the minimum output is {{k}}.
The left endpoint is farther from the vertex than the right endpoint, giving q({{lo}})={{yleft}} and q({{hi}})={{yright}}.
Because the parabola opens upward, the restricted range is [{{k}},{{yleft}}].

attemptFeedback: Do not assume the right endpoint gives the largest output; compare distances from the vertex.
supportHints: For an upward-opening parabola, farther horizontal distance from the vertex gives a larger output.

documents.prompt: For $g(x)=-{{a}}(x-{{h}})^2{{k|signed}}$, a student writes the range as $[{{k}},\infty)$ because the vertex y-value is {{k}}. Correct the range in interval notation.

solutionReview.headline: The vertex is a maximum when the parabola opens downward.
reasoning: The negative leading coefficient makes every other output less than or equal to {{k}}.
Therefore the range extends downward without bound and includes {{k}}: $(-\infty,{{k}}]$.

attemptFeedback: First decide whether the vertex is a minimum or maximum.
supportHints: Opening downward means the vertex is the greatest y-value.

documents.prompt: A quadratic has domain all real numbers, opens upward, and has vertex $({{h}},{{k}})$. Write its range in interval notation and give the inequality statement that describes the same y-values.

solutionReview.headline: The same range can be represented as an interval or as an inequality.
reasoning: Opening upward makes {{k}} the minimum output.
The vertex is included, so the range is $[{{k}},\infty)$, equivalently $y\ge {{k}}$.

attemptFeedback: Both representations must say that y is greater than or equal to the vertex output.
supportHints: Upward-opening quadratics have a minimum at the vertex.

variants.prompt: An upward-opening quadratic has vertex $({{h}},{{k}})$. Student A writes the range as $[{{k}},\infty)$. Student B writes $y\ge{{k}}$. Decide whether the two statements represent the SAME set of outputs, explain the role of the included vertex, and give both representations.

responseFields.label: Are the two range statements equivalent?

choices.label: Yes; both include {{k}} and all larger y-values.
No; interval notation and inequality notation describe different sets.
The vertex is on the graph, so y={{k}} is actually attained.
The graph only approaches y={{k}} but never reaches it.

solutionReview.headline: Equivalent representations should describe exactly the same attainable outputs.
reasoning: The upward-opening quadratic has minimum output {{k}} at its vertex.
Because the vertex is part of the graph, {{k}} is included.
Thus [{{k}},∞) and y≥{{k}} describe the same range.

attemptFeedback: Compare which y-values each notation includes rather than comparing the symbols visually.
supportHints: A bracket at {{k}} corresponds to ≥ because the minimum is attained.
